rule.docs:
Summary

- Name: noUselessUndefinedInitialization
- Fix: safe
- Default severity: info
- Available from version: 1.7.2
- Diagnostic category: lint/complexity/noUselessUndefinedInitialization
- This rule is recommended

Description

 Disallow initializing variables to `undefined`.

 A variable that is declared and not initialized to any value automatically gets the value of `undefined`.
 It’s considered a best practice to avoid initializing variables to `undefined`.

 Please note that any inline comments attached to the initialization value or variable will be moved at the end of the variable declaration on auto-fix.
 Please be also aware that this differs from Eslint's behaviour.

Examples

Invalid

 ```js,expect_diagnostic
 var a = undefined;
 ```
 ```js,expect_diagnostic
 let b = undefined, c = 1, d = 2;
 ```
 ```js,expect_diagnostic
 for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
 	let i = undefined;
 }
 ```
 ```js,expect_diagnostic
 let f = /**/undefined/**/ ;
 ```
Valid

 ```js
 var a = 1;
 ```
 ```js
 class Foo {
 	bar = undefined;
 }
 ```

 Exported variables are not flagged because in some frameworks (e.g., Svelte 4),
 initializing exported variables to `undefined` is used to declare optional props.

 ```js
 export let x = undefined;
 ```
 ```js
 let y = undefined;
 export { y };
 ```

analysis.summary: Flags initializations where a variable is explicitly set to `undefined`, since uninitialized variables already have that value.
firingShapes: for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { let j = undefined; }
function f() { let x = undefined; return x; }
analysis.fixDescription: Removes the `= undefined` initializer from the variable declaration, leaving only the declaration (and any other declarators in the same statement), preserving leading/trailing whitespace but moving any inline comments attached to the initializer or declarator to the end of the full declaration statement.
hazards: In a `for` loop initializer like `for (let i = 0, j = undefined; i < n; i++)`, removing `j = undefined` changes the loop step syntax if `j` is the last declarator, potentially creating invalid syntax.
If the variable is declared in a comma expression such as `(x = 1, y = undefined)`, removing `= undefined` alters the expression’s value and side-effect timing.
In destructuring patterns like `[a = undefined] = []`, removing the default value changes matching behavior when the source array has fewer elements.

When the initializer is part of a larger expression like `if ((let x = undefined) === null)`, the removal breaks grammar because `let` cannot appear in that position without an initializer in older syntax interpretations.

If the variable name is `undefined` itself (e.g., `let undefined = 42;` in non-strict mode), the fix would leave `let undefined;` which is a syntax error in strict mode and changes meaning in sloppy mode.
In conditional declarations like `if (true) let x = undefined;`, the autofix produces `if (true) let x;` which is invalid syntax because `let` declarations in statement position require a block.
When the declaration includes a trailing comma like `let a = undefined,`, removing the initializer leaves `let a,` which is a syntax error due to the dangling comma.

If the variable is declared in a `with` object property initializer like `with ({ get x() { return undefined } }) let x = undefined;`, removing the initializer may affect lookup timing due to changes in when the binding is instantiated.

In cases where the initializer contains a comment with a closing brace like `let x = undefined /* } */ ;`, moving the comment to the end of the statement could unintentionally comment out subsequent code if not properly wrapped.

If the declaration is the sole content of a loop body like `for (; ;) let x = undefined;`, the fix results in `for (; ;) let x;` which is invalid because `let` declarations cannot appear directly in loop bodies without a block.

results.title: null/undefined distinction affecting optional chaining
results.hazard: Removing `= undefined` changes initialization timing, causing optional chaining to short-circuit incorrectly due to ReferenceError instead of undefined.

findings.detail: model expected the rule to fire, it stayed silent

results.title: Order of evaluation with comma operator and side effects
results.hazard: Removing initializer deletes a side-effect expression in a comma sequence, altering evaluation order and omitting a function call.

diagnostics.message: It's not necessary to initialize b to undefined.

results.title: Comment displacement changing source meaning
results.hazard: Moving an inline comment after declaration alters its interpretation—here, turning a TODO into dead code via accidental line comment.
